title: Prilocaine plasma levels and methemoglobinemia in patients undergoing tumescent liposuction involving less than 2,000 ml.
abstract:
As a reaction to reported adverse outcomes after lidocaine infiltration in tumescent liposuction, prilocaine has gained increasing popularity. Previous studies investigating large-volume liposuction procedures found maximum prilocaine levels and methemoglobinemia up to 12 h postoperatively, suggesting that liposuction should be performed as a hospital procedure only. The aim of this study was to determine prilocaine plasma levels and methemoglobinemia in patients after low- to average-volume liposuction for the purpose of defining the required postoperative surveillance period.

In 25 patients undergoing liposuction involving less than 2,000 ml prilocaine levels and methemoglobinemia were measured over 4 h postoperatively. Liposuction was conducted after the tumescent technique using a [dose figure omitted] hypotonic prilocaine solution with epinephrine.

The average prilocaine dose was [dose figure omitted], with a maximum dose of [dose figure omitted]. The peak prilocaine plasma level of [dose figure omitted] occurred 3 h after the infiltration. The mean methemoglobinemia at this time point was [dose figure omitted]. Only one patient demonstrated a slightly elevated methemoglobin level of [dose figure omitted], but lacked any clinical signs of methemoglobinemia. The prilocaine recovery in the aspirate averaged 36 +/- 4%, indicating that a large amount is removed by suctioning.

The patients did not experience high plasma levels of prilocaine or methemoglobinemia undergoing liposuction involving less than 2,000 ml using a [dose figure omitted] hypotonic prilocaine solution. The authors therefore conclude that this procedure can be performed safely with a monitoring period of 12 h.
